extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants and patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Standardized MPEP form paragraphs and examiner guidance for making rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (and pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph), including common bases for indefiniteness and omissions and instructions on paragraph usage and explanatory content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 112(b) and pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, Second Paragraph (¶ 7.30.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of the statutory text of 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (and pre-AIA second paragraph): the specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the inventor (or applicant pre-AIA) regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) The statute need not be re‑cited in all Office actions — required in first actions on the merits and final rejections; where not cited use paragraph 7.103. (2) Paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.30.02 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Claim Inventor’s Invention (¶ 7.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA second paragraph) as failing to set forth the subject matter which the inventor/joint inventor (or applicant pre‑AIA) regards as the invention; evidence that the claim(s) fail to correspond in scope with that which the inventor regards as the invention can be found in a reply or other submission by the inventor/applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) Use only where inventor/applicant has stated (outside the application as filed) that the invention is different from what is defined in the claim(s). (3) In bracket 3 identify the submission and its filing date. (4) In bracket 4 set forth what the inventor/applicant stated. (5) In bracket 5 explain how that statement indicates an invention other than what is being claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim (Indefinite) (¶ 7.34.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA second paragraph) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter the inventor/applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) Insert proper claim numbering/grammar; review dependent claims for same defect and add if necessary. (3) Follow this paragraph with one or more of form paragraphs 7.34.02–7.34.10 and/or 7.34.23–7.34.24 as applicable; if none appropriate, supply a full explanation identifying particular term(s)/limitation(s) rendering the claim indefinite and why. If one of ordinary skill can determine the scope, do not use this rejection. See MPEP §§2171–2174. See form paragraph 7.34.15 for pro se applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology Used Inconsistent with Accepted Meaning (¶ 7.34.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant acts as his/her own lexicographer to specifically define a claim term contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the claim term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice that the applicant intended to so redefine that claim term. The term '[1]' in claim [2] is used by the claim to mean '[3]' while the accepted meaning is '[4]'; the term is indefinite because the specification does not clearly redefine the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) In bracket 3, point out the applicant‑assigned meaning taking into account the entire disclosure. (2) In bracket 4, point out accepted meaning and support via textbook/dictionary citation; see MPEP §2173.05(a). (3) Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01. (4) Use only where the specification does not clearly redefine the claim term at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Term — Term of Degree Rendering Claim Indefinite (¶ 7.34.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term '[1]' in claim [2] is a relative term (term of degree) which renders the claim indefinite because the term is not defined by the claim, the specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree, and one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of the scope of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) In bracket 3 explain which parameter, quantity, or other limitation in the claim has been rendered indefinite by the term. (2) This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Range/Limitation And Narrow Range/Limitation in Same Claim (¶ 7.34.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range or limitation (in the same claim) may be indefinite if the resulting claim does not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the patent protection desired. Example: claim [1] recites the broad recitation [2] and also recites [3], the narrower statement; the claim(s) are indefinite because there is doubt whether the narrower language is merely exemplary or a required feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) In bracket 2 insert broader range/limitation and where it appears; in bracket 3 insert narrower and where it appears. This paragraph may be modified to fit other indefiniteness instances. (2) Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01. See MPEP §2173.05(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Antecedent Basis in the Claims (¶ 7.34.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] recites the limitation [2] in [3]. There is insufficient antecedent basis for this limitation in the claim (e.g., 'said lever' or 'the lever' without prior introduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) In bracket 2 insert the limitation lacking antecedent basis; (2) in bracket 3 identify where in the claim the limitation appears; (3) Use this form paragraph ONLY in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes scope indeterminate. It must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Are a Literal Translation (¶ 7.34.07)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are generally narrative and indefinite, failing to conform with current U.S. practice; they appear to be a literal translation into English from a foreign document and are replete with grammatical and idiomatic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'For Example' (¶ 7.34.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'for example' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitation(s) following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2173.05(d). Examiner Note: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Or The Like' (¶ 7.34.09)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'or the like' renders the claim(s) indefinite because the claim(s) include(s) elements not actually disclosed (those encompassed by 'or the like'), thereby rendering the scope of the claim(s) unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2173.05(d). Examiner Note: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Such As' (¶ 7.34.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'such as' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2173.05(d). Examiner Note: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Steps Omitted (¶ 7.34.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA) as being incomplete for omitting essential steps, such omission amounting to a gap between the steps. The omitted steps are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) In bracket 2, recite the steps omitted from the claims. (3) Give the rationale for considering the omitted steps critical/essential and explain basis for concluding inventor regards the omitted matter as essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements Omitted (¶ 7.34.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA) as being incomplete for omitting essential elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the elements. The omitted elements are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) In bracket 2, recite the elements omitted from the claims. (3) Give the rationale for considering the omitted elements critical/essential and explain basis for concluding inventor regards the omitted matter as essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted (¶ 7.34.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA) as being incomplete for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the necessary structural connections. The omitted structural cooperative relationships are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) In bracket 2, recite the omitted structural cooperative relationships of elements. (3) Give the rationale for considering these cooperative relationships critical/essential and explain basis for concluding inventor regards them as essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. 112, Pro Se (¶ 7.34.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as failing to define the invention in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA second paragraph). The claim(s) are narrative in form and replete with indefinite language; the structure making up the device must be clearly and positively specified and organized to present a complete operative device. Claims must be in one sentence form only; note the format of claims in cited patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when applicant is pro se; provides guidance on required claim form and clarity for pro se filers. See form paragraph usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim — Omnibus Claim (¶ 7.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA) as being indefinite in that it fails to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language. This claim is an omnibus type claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (2) Use this paragraph to reject an 'omnibus' type claim — no further explanation necessary. (3) Example of an omnibus claim: 'A device substantially as shown and described.' See form paragraph 7.34.01 for related procedural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation in the Claim (¶ 7.35.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contains the trademark/trade name [2]. Where a trademark or trade name is used in a claim as a limitation to identify or describe a particular material or product, the claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA); the claim scope is uncertain since a trademark/trade name identifies a source of goods, not the goods themselves, and thus does not properly identify or describe the goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) In bracket 2, insert the trademark/trade name and where it is used in the claim. (2) In bracket 3, specify the material or product which is intended to be identified/ described by the trademark/trade name. Cite Ex parte Simpson, 218 USPQ 1020 (Bd. App. 1982). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103 where applicable.
